name.en: Fake airline message: flight changed or points expiring

how.en: Scammers pretend to be airlines, airports, travel agents or accommodation providers. A message says your flight was cancelled or your booking changed, that your reward points are about to expire, or offers a free gift. It pushes you to click a link, call a number or pay urgently. The link goes to a fake login or payment page that steals your account or card details. Fake “customer support” accounts on WhatsApp do the same.

text.en: A message claims to be from your airline, an airport or a booking site.
It says your flight changed or your points will expire soon.
It asks you to click a link or call a number to sort it out.
The fake page asks for your login or card details, or an urgent payment.
Qantas Frequent Flyer: 18,400 points expire on 30 Nov. Redeem them now for a free gift before they are lost: [link]

en: An unexpected message asking you to click or call about a booking.
Points that are “about to expire” and a free gift.
Urgent requests to pay or share passport or card details.
Use the airline’s app or official website, or a number you find yourself.
Don’t use links or contact details from the message.
If you entered card details, contact your bank.
